description.value: Great Bear Chalet is an intimate, all-inclusive wilderness retreat on the banks of the Atnarko River inside Tweedsmuir Provincial Park, accommodating a maximum of four guests in two private queen-bedroom suites with ensuites. The property operates entirely off-grid and is best known for guided grizzly bear viewing, eco-river drifts, and interpretive hikes through one of BC's most significant salmon and grizzly habitats. Hosts and accredited guides Jefferson and Bindi Bray have been immersing guests in this ecosystem for over 20 years.

address.value: 8080 Mackenzie Highway, Tweedsmuir Provincial Park, BC V0T 1H0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is fully accessible and provides detailed information about the chalet's facilities and services. Laundry service and WiFi are explicitly listed under 'Included Services' on the Chalet page. No mention of cycling, bike storage, or any cycling-related amenities appears anywhere on the site; the property is a luxury wildlife-viewing retreat targeting grizzly bear tourism, not cycling tourism. Contact details (phone, address) were sourced from the /contact-us/ subpage since OSM carried no contact fields.
concerns: OSM record contains almost no tags beyond name and tourism=guest_house; phone, address, and email were absent from OSM and sourced solely from the website.
No cycling-related content, amenities, or services mentioned anywhere on the website — property is focused exclusively on grizzly bear wildlife tourism.
Very remote location inside Tweedsmuir Provincial Park; road access and cycling infrastructure context are unknown.
All-inclusive exclusive model (max 4 guests) may be incompatible with drop-in touring cyclist needs.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a legitimate, operating BC accommodation, but it is a highly exclusive luxury wildlife retreat (max 4 guests, all-inclusive grizzly bear focus) with no mention of cycling, bike storage, or cycling-oriented services anywhere on the site. Neither required WWC criterion can be confirmed, and its primary audience is wildlife tourists rather than touring cyclists.
